title: Two Colleagues Argue About Fitness Trackers
script: Larasati: [thoughtful] Wisnu, you checked your watch again. Are you obsessed with your heart rate now?
Wisnu: I'm not obsessed, I'm informed. This thing tells me exactly how well I recovered from yesterday's session, down to the percentage.
Larasati: [carefully] Does a percentage actually tell you anything useful, though, or does it just give you something new to worry about?
Wisnu: It tells me whether I should push hard today or take it easier, which frankly beats guessing based on how tired I feel.
Larasati: [reflective] I'd argue how tired you feel is precisely the information worth listening to, rather than outsourcing that judgment to an algorithm.
Wisnu: Fair point, except my own judgment has talked me into overtraining more than once, whereas the data has never lied to me.
Larasati: [honestly] Has it ever made you anxious, though? I've heard people describe feeling almost punished by a bad sleep score.
Wisnu: Occasionally, yes. There was a stretch last month when a low readiness score genuinely ruined my morning before I'd even left bed.
Larasati: [gently] That's exactly what worries me. A number decided how your day would feel before anything had happened.
Wisnu: When you frame it that way, it does sound slightly absurd, letting a wristband dictate my mood before breakfast.
Larasati: [calmly] I'm not saying throw it away, just that it shouldn't be the only voice you listen to.
Wisnu: What would you suggest instead, given you clearly think I've handed over too much authority to a gadget?
Larasati: [encouraging] Treat the data as one opinion among several, alongside how your body actually feels and what your week realistically allows.
Wisnu: That's reasonable. I suppose I started trusting the number more than myself somewhere along the way, without really noticing.
Larasati: [seriously] Most of us do, eventually, with something. At least you're willing to question it instead of defending it blindly.
Wisnu: Don't get used to this humility, though. I'm still checking my recovery score the second we finish this conversation.
Larasati: Naturally. Just promise me you'll ignore it occasionally, as an act of rebellion against your own wrist.
Wisnu: Deal. Though if I sleep badly tonight, I reserve the right to blame you for the data.
